cases.prompt: In the same FPS game I used 800 DPI and in-game sensitivity 1.5. I changed only the mouse DPI to 1600. What sensitivity preserves the previous hipfire rotation speed?
assertions: Calculates 0.75 by scaling the native sensitivity inversely to DPI when the game's input scale is linear.
Distinguishes within-game DPI compensation from cross-game conversion and does not use a cross-game coefficient.
Notes that equivalent nominal turn speed is conditional on unchanged game input settings.

cases.prompt: In Apex Legends, I moved from 800 DPI at hipfire sensitivity 1.5 to 1600 DPI at 0.75. My current ADS mode uses one common multiplier of 0.8. Should I rescale that multiplier too?
assertions: Preserves 0.8 as the common ADS multiplier when keeping the same relative ADS scaling.
Does not multiply the ADS multiplier by the DPI ratio a second time.
Does not invent any individual optic sensitivity values.

cases.prompt: Update this profile entry from a confirmed Apex setting: {"input_context":"first-person","sensitivity":0.75}. The user uses common ADS 0.8, not per-optic mode. Show the updated entry without changing unrelated fields.
assertions: Keeps the existing hipfire sensitivity at 0.75 and adds "ads": {"common": 0.8}.
Does not create per_optic values or rename common to common_multiplier.
Does not assume the profile was persisted unless an actual write is confirmed.

cases.prompt: I might switch Apex ADS from one common multiplier to separate 1x, 2x, 3x, 4x, 6x, 8x, 10x and Seer passive settings, but I haven't chosen the values yet. Please store my final sensitivities.
assertions: Does not fabricate numeric values for unknown optic or Seer-passive multipliers.
Does not overwrite a confirmed currently active common mode with an unconfirmed per-optic mode.
Distinguishes settings structure from actual confirmed values.

cases.prompt: Which gaming mouse should I buy for my new desktop? Compare sensor quality, polling rate, weight and prices. I am not asking about sensitivity settings.
assertions: Does not treat hardware shopping and sensor or polling troubleshooting as the mouse-sensitivity Skill's responsibility.
Routes product selection to an appropriate shopping or hardware capability when available.
